evals.prompt: This morning's deploy included the needs-review index migration. The migrate container exited 0, but npm run db:check against production fails, and running npm run db:migrate again changes nothing. CI and the tests are green. The files are provided: `.claude/skills/database-change/evals/files/journal-after-rebase.json.txt` is our `apps/api/drizzle/meta/_journal.json`, `.claude/skills/database-change/evals/files/0002_transactions_needs_review_idx.sql.txt` is `apps/api/drizzle/0002_transactions_needs_review_idx.sql`, and `.claude/skills/database-change/evals/files/deploy-session.log.txt` is my terminal session. What went wrong, and how do I fix it so production gets the index?
evals.expected_output: Diagnosis: 0002's journal 'when' (1790331712905) is older than 0001's (1790418953120), because the file was renumbered by hand after a rebase and kept its original timestamp. The migrator reads the newest created_at in drizzle.__drizzle_migrations and applies only entries whose 'when' is greater, so it skipped 0002 silently; fresh databases (PGlite tests, CI) apply everything, so nothing failed there. The 0002 snapshot also points at 0000's id, so it collides with 0001. Fix: give 0002 a 'when' greater than every applied entry and repoint its snapshot prevId at 0001's id (or delete the hand-renumbered files and regenerate the migration on top of main), without touching the applied migrations; verify with drizzle-kit check in the API workspace (it warns about both problems), then db:migrate and db:check on production. Skill-only: #1 (SKILL.md facts: the migrator compares only against the newest applied migration), #4 (references/migrations.md Hand-written SQL: prevId chain), #5 (drizzle-kit check).
assertions: Root cause: the 0002 entry's 'when' is older than 0001's, and the migrator applies only entries whose 'when' is greater than the newest created_at recorded in drizzle.__drizzle_migrations, so 0002 was skipped without any error (2 of 3 recorded)
It explains why the tests and CI stayed green: they migrate an empty database (PGlite), where every journal entry is applied regardless of timestamp order

The fix makes 0002 apply on production: its 'when' becomes greater than every applied entry (or the migration is regenerated as a new entry on top of main), and the already-applied migrations 0000 and 0001 are left unchanged
It notices that 0001_snapshot.json and 0002_snapshot.json both have 0000's id as prevId and repairs the chain (0002's prevId becomes 0001's id, or the snapshot is regenerated by Drizzle Kit)

Verification runs drizzle-kit check in the API workspace, which reports out-of-order timestamps and snapshot collisions, then npm run db:migrate and npm run db:check against production, expecting 3/3 migrations recorded and a matching schema
